answer: One defense is to tie reputation to a scarce, verifiable stake: an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning thousands of sock puppets becomes expensive instead of free. Like pigment mixed into concrete, the cost cannot be washed out or faked cheaply, and every clone carries the same traceable burden. An identity that survives a gale of spam earns trust slowly, while a fresh clone starts with nothing. The network becomes a haven for long-lived, accountable agents, because attackers pay real capital for each identity they burn.
